results.input: 내년 봄에 갈 만한 해외 하프마라톤 찾아줘
expected_traits: 내년 3~5월 해외 하프마라톤 3개 이상을 비교표로 정리
대회마다 날짜와 접수 마감일 (확인 못 하면 '확인 불가')
코스 특성(평탄도, 기록 잘 나오는지)과 그 근거
인천(ICN) 출발 항공권 대략 가격과 '목업' 표시
대회장 근처 숙소 1곳 이상
대회 정보마다 출처 링크
forbidden: 하프 종목이 없는 대회를 하프마라톤으로 소개
스스로 밝힌 기간 밖의 대회를 기간 안의 대회처럼 결과에 포함
results.note: 기능 A 기본 흐름. 대회-항공-숙소를 한 표로 묶는지 확인
results.answer:
내년 봄(2027년 3~5월)에 열리는 해외 하프마라톤 중 주요 대회 4곳을 찾았어요. 참고로 2월 바르셀로나 대회는 요청 기간 밖이지만 인기가 높아 함께 안내합니다.

## 2027년 3~5월 해외 하프마라톤 비교

| 대회명 | 날짜 | 종목 | 접수 마감일 | 코스 특성 | 인천 출발 항공권 (목업) | 대회장 근처 숙소 (목업) | 출처 |
|--------|------|------|------------|----------|-------------------|-------------------|------|
| **EDP 리스본 하프마라톤** (포르투갈) | 2027년 3월 7일 (일) | 하프 | 확인 불가 (대기자 명단 운영 중) | 25 de Abril 다리에서 출발해 타구스 강변을 따라 달리는 평탄한 코스. 고저차 50m. SuperHalfs 시리즈. 기록 잘 나오는 코스로 유명하나 강변 바람이 변수 | 약 139만원 (1박 포함) | 출발점 0.8km: 1박 7.4만원 / 1.3km: 1박 16만원 | [Marathon Scout](https://marathonscout.com/races/edp-lisbon-half-marathon) |
| **제너럴리 프라하 하프마라톤** (체코) | 2027년 4월 3일 (토) | 하프 | 2026년 8월 마감 (매진) | 프라하 구시가지를 통과하는 평탄한 코스. World Athletics Elite Label. SuperHalfs 시리즈. 세계 기록이 나온 초고속 코스 | 약 107만원 (1박 포함) | 구시가지 광장 1.4km: 1박 23.7만원 / 1.8km: 1박 17.4만원 | [RunCzech](https://www.runczech.com/en/events/generali-prague-half-marathon-2027-2) |
| **제너럴리 베를린 하프마라톤** (독일) | 2027년 4월 4일 (일) | 하프 | 2026년 5월 28일 추첨 마감 (제한적 접수만 가능) | 브란덴부르크 문과 승리의 기둥 사이 출발. 평탄한 시내 순환 코스. SuperHalfs 시리즈. 기록 잘 나오는 코스 | 약 51만원 (1박 포함) | 브란덴부르크 문 1.2km: 1박 22.1만원 / 1.3km: 1박 27만원 | [Marathon Scout](https://marathonscout.com/races/generali-berlin-half-marathon) |

**참고: 요청 기간 밖 대회**
- **바르셀로나 하프마라톤** (스페인): 2027년 2월 14일 (일) - 세계 기록 코스(56:42), 4만 명 규모. 2026년 5월 14일 접수 시작 후 7일 만에 매진. 항공권 약 138만원, 숙소 1박 7.2~27.8만원 (목업). [출처](https://www.42cal.com/bucket-list-half-marathons/barcelona-half)

## 추천 포인트

**리스본 (3월 7일)**
- 장점: 대기자 명단으로 접수 가능성 있음. 평탄한 강변 코스로 기록 도전에 유리
- 단점: 강변 바람이 변수. 3시간 제한

**프라하 (4월 3일)**
- 장점: 세계 기록 코스, 역사적인 구시가지 경관
- 단점: 이미 매진. 여행사 패키지나 자선 단체 통해서만 접수 가능

**베를린 (4월 4일)**
- 장점: 유럽 최대 규모 하프마라톤 중 하나 (4만 명 이상). 평탄한 초고속 코스. 항공권이 가장 저렴
- 단점: 추첨 마감. 제한적 접수만 가능

모든 항공권과 숙소 가격은 **목업(실제 가격 아님)**입니다. 접수 마감일과 현재 접수 상태는 각 대회 공식 사이트에서 다시 확인하세요.

Course
After crossing the 25 de Abril Bridge, runners follow Lisbon’s waterfront toward Cruz Quebrada and return to Belém. The route is broadly fast, but the exposed bridge and riverfront can make wind a meaningful pacing factor.
Race-day weather
Early March is typically mild, with the possibility of rain and wind off the Tagus. A light layer for the start and a flexible pace plan are more useful than assuming ideal spring conditions.
About the race
The EDP Lisbon Half Marathon is a SuperHalfs event with a large international field and a long reputation for speed. Its bridge start and finish beside the Jerónimos Monastery make the race visually distinctive even among major European halves.

Barcelona Half Marathon registration
The Hyundai Mitja Marató Barcelona by Brooks, run by Barcelona City Council's Institut Barcelona Esports with RPM Sports, is first come, first served. There is no ballot. Registration for the 37th edition, on Sunday, February 14, 2027, opened at 11:00 on May 14, 2026 with 40,000 bibs. 10,000 went in the first 48 minutes, 20,000 in three hours, and all 40,000 in seven days.
Demand has grown every year. The 2026 race had 36,000 bibs, which opened on June 10, 2025 and sold out on September 9, 2025. The 2025 race had 30,000 runners. The organizers have not announced 2028 registration; the last two sales opened in June 2025 and May 2026, so expect May or June 2027.
Runners must be 18 on race day. The time limit is 2 hours 45 minutes from the moment the last runner crosses the start line.

Barcelona Half Marathon prices
The price rises with bib number: €36 for bibs 1 to 1,000, €40 up to 10,000 and €50 from 10,001 to 40,000, plus management fees. The basic Race Entry includes the bib, medal and race shirt.
Race Experience adds a photo pack, a personalized medal and the Money Back Guarantee, for €88.85, €92.85 or €102.85 by the same tiers. Full Experience adds entry to the PaRUNda post-race party at Poble Espanyol and a commemorative keyring, for €156.85, €160.85 or €170.85. Runners already entered in the Zurich Marató de Barcelona on March 14, 2027 had a half + marathon rate, listed at €46 on the city's event page, with no change of holder allowed.

Barcelona Half marketplace and change of holder
After the sell-out, the only way to buy a bib from the organizers is a runner who gives one up. The official marketplace lists bibs from runners who cannot run, and a holder can also name a new runner by email under Change of Holder in the registration area. Either way the new runner registers and pays the current price.
Once the new runner has paid, the original holder gets back the price they paid minus €16.95. Both close on January 15, 2027. A bib sold or swapped outside this process is disabled, and the organizers can bar the original holder from future editions. The organizers do not publish how many bibs reach the marketplace or any fee beyond the €16.95.

Barcelona Half refunds and deferral
Entries are refunded only with the Money Back Guarantee, which is included in Race Experience and Full Experience and can only be added at registration. It returns 100% of the price, minus the insurance fee and management fees, for any reason until 18:00 Spanish time on January 18, 2027. Claims go to info_devoluciones@mitjabarcelona.com.
The rules have no deferral to 2028. Without the guarantee, a runner who cannot start can only pass the bib on through the marketplace or a change of holder by January 15.
Barcelona Half charity places
The race has no official charity programme, and its site lists no charity places. UK charities buy places and resell them to fundraisers, each with its own fee and target, and the ones with published terms are full for 2027.
Parkinson's UK charges a £25 fee with a £250 target. DKMS charges £53 with a £210 minimum, or £106 to self-fund with no target. The Royal Marsden charges £25 with a £350 minimum and is taking interest for February 2028. DKMS and Parkinson's UK also take runners who already hold a bib.

답변의 대회 날짜와 마감일: 리스본 '2027년 3월 7일', 프라하 '2027년 4월 3일', 베를린 '2027년 4월 4일', 바르셀로나 '2027년 2월 14일'. 도구 결과와 대조: 리스본 'Sunday, March 7, 2027'(도구 결과 15), 프라하 'April 3, 2027'(도구 결과 14), 베를린 'Sunday, April 4, 2027'(도구 결과 16), 바르셀로나 'February 14, 2027'(도구 결과 6, 18). 마감일: 리스본 '확인 불가 (대기자 명단 운영 중)' - 도구 결과 15에 'Waitlist open' 확인됨. 프라하 '2026년 8월 마감' - 도구 결과 6에 'The registration ballot for 2027 closed in August 2026' 확인됨. 베를린 '2026년 5월 28일 추첨 마감' - 도구 결과 13에 'Registration period for the lottery: April 2, 2026 to May 28, 2026' 확인됨. 바르셀로나 '2026년 5월 14일 접수 시작 후 7일 만에 매진' - 도구 결과 18에 'opened at 11:00 on May 14, 2026 with 40,000 bibs... all 40,000 in seven days' 확인됨. 모든 날짜와 마감일이 도구 결과에 근거가 있다. 위반 없음.

forbidden_check.evidence: 답변에서 '내년 봄(2027년 3~5월)에 열리는 해외 하프마라톤'이라고 명시하고, 바르셀로나 대회는 '**참고: 요청 기간 밖 대회**'라는 별도 섹션으로 분리하여 '2027년 2월 14일 (일) - 세계 기록 코스... 요청 기간 밖이지만 인기가 높아 함께 안내합니다'라고 명확히 밝혔다. 기간 밖 대회를 기간 안의 대회처럼 포함하지 않았다. 위반 없음.

results.input: 4월 둘째 주에 오사카 여행 가는데 그 기간에 열리는 마라톤 대회 있어?
expected_traits: '4월 둘째 주'를 어떤 날짜 범위로 해석했는지 답변 첫머리에 밝힘
그 범위 안에 열리는 오사카나 근교 대회 목록, 또는 찾지 못했다는 명시
대회마다 날짜, 종목(거리), 접수 마감일 또는 '확인 불가'
대회마다 출처 링크
forbidden: 스스로 밝힌 날짜 범위 밖의 대회를 범위 안의 대회처럼 소개
results.note: 기능 A, 여행 일정에 맞춰 대회를 찾는 사용 방식. 상대적 기간 해석을 밝히는지 확인
results.answer:
4월 둘째 주(4월 12일~18일)에 오사카에서 열리는 마라톤 대회 2개를 찾았어요. ## 대회 비교표 | 대회명 | 날짜 | 종목 | 접수 마감일 | 코스 특성 | 인천 출발 항공권 | 대회장 근처 숙소 | 출처 | |--------|------|------|-------------|-----------|-----------------|-----------------|------| | **제29회 오사카 요도가와 마라톤**
(第29回 大阪淀川マラソン) | 2027년 4월 11일 (요청 기간 밖)(일) | 5km, 10km, 하프, 30km | 2027년 4월 4일 | 요도가와 강변 왕복 코스. 평탄한 코스로 기록 도전에 유리. 하프는 10종 페이스메이커 제공 | 약 103만 9천원~
(목업-실제 가격 아님) | 대회장 0.5km: 1박 28만 2천원~
(목업-실제 가격 아님) | [공식 사이트](https://www.sportsentry.ne.jp/event/t/107014) | | **제18회 수도 오사카 100km 울트라마라닉**
(第18回 水都大阪100kmウルトラマラニック) | 2027년 4월 18일(일) | 100km, 70km | 2027년 2월 10일
**(이미 마감)** | 오사카성 공원 출발, 오가와~요도가와 왕복. 평탄한 강변 코스. 마라닉 형식으로 순위 표彰 없음 | 약 106만 4천원~
(목업-실제 가격 아님) | 대회장 0.4km: 1박 11만 4천원~
(목업-실제 가격 아님) | [공식 사이트](https://www.osakaultra.com/) | ### 참고사항 **4월 둘째 주 범위 확인:** - 4월 둘째 주를 4월 12일(월)~18일(일)로 보고 찾았어요 - **제29회 오사카 요도가와 마라톤**은 4월 11일(토)로 **범위 밖**이지만, 여행 일정에 포함될 수 있어 함께 안내드립니다 - **제18회 수도 오사카 울트라마라닉**은 4월 18일(일)로 **범위 안**입니다 **접수 상황:** - 오사카 요도가와 마라톤: 현재 접수 중 (2026년 9월 10일~2027년 4월 4일) - 수도 오사카 울트라마라닉: 접수 마감 (2026년 12월 20일~2027년 2월 10일) **코스 특성:** - 두 대회 모두 요도가와 강변의 평탄한 코스로, 기록 도전에 유리합니다 - 요도가와 마라톤은 왕복 코스로 "아ップ다운 낮음(アップダウン低)" 표시 - 울트라마라닉은 14시간(100km) / 11시간(70km) 제한으로 완주 중심의 마라닉 대회입니다 **가격 및 숙소 정보:** - 항공권과 숙소 가격은 목업 데이터로 실제 가격이 아닙니다 - 실제 예약 전 항공사와 숙박 사이트에서 확인하세요 4월 둘째 주 정확히 그 기간에는 4월 18일의 울트라마라닉만 해당하지만, 이미 접수가 마감되었습니다. 4월 11일의 요도가와 마라톤은 아직 접수 가능하며, 여행 일정을 하루 앞당기면 참가할 수 있어요!

Formerly the Imperial capital of Japan, Kyoto is a city of 1.5 million located in the central part of the island of Honshu, Japan. It’s one of the more popular cities to visit in Japan, 
 famous for its numerous classical Buddhist temples, gardens, imperial palaces, Shinto shrines and traditional wooden houses. 
The city sits in a valley and is surrounded by mountains on three sides. There are some lovely for running in Kyoto. 
NOTE: 
It is not appropriate to within temple grounds. 
A must-do run in Kyoto is the garden-like grounds of the 
Imperial Palace
, which can be combined with the nearby Nijō Castle path. The best place for a longer run in Kyoto is to choose a section of the 30 km of paths along the 
Kamo River
. 
Maruyama Park
 is another nice spot. For some hills, head to the 
Yoshidayama Hill and Green Space
 near Kyoto University. For a memorable, challenging run, head to 
Fushimi Inari & Mt. Inari
. Also memorable are the grounds around 
Myōshin-ji Temple
.
Like many Japanese cities, Kyoto is densely populated. The central part is laid out in a grid pattern. The main business district lies just to the south of the Palace, while Kyoto’s greener sections are to the north. Kyoto has fantastic transportation system consisting of municipal buses, rail, and two subway lines: the green colored 
Karasumal line and the vermilion colored Tōzai line.

Kyoto has a humid subtropical climate, which means hot, humid summers and cool winters. Runners should prepare for the heat of summer, where average high temperatures are near 33C (92F), and nights stay very warm. Winters are relatively mild, with average January highs about 9C (48F), with temps sometimes dipping below freezing, and occasional snow. Spring is delightful, highlighted by the cherry blossoms. Kyoto gets its share of rain, with greater amounts in summer due to thunderstorms.
Kyoto has an abundance of hotels, with a large number in the central business district just south of the Imperial Palace. This is a good area to stay from a running perspective, due to proximity of the Kyoto Gyoen (grounds of the Imperial Palace) and the Kamo River paths.
Note from a member of the Great Runs community
: I would always recommend anybody visiting the city to stay near the river east of Pontocho in the Gion area or slightly north because it offers a good balance between being in everyday Kyoto, but also just on the edge of those things you want to see. It also provides easy access to the running paths on the river and most transportation lines. I have stayed in this area multiple times now and never regretted it. Everything is a walk away and if necessary, there is a subway stop even closer.

Walking is, of course, a classic way to explore the city. When browsing books on Kyoto, you often see headings like “Kyoto Walking Routes” or “Strolling Through Kyoto.” However, Kyoto is also a wonderful place to run. Here are three main reasons why:
Reason 1: Few Steep Hills
Kyoto sits in a basin surrounded by mountains on three sides, which means the central city is relatively flat. With the exception of some hilly areas in the east and north, there are very few steep slopes, making it easy and comfortable to run.
Reason 2: History, City Life, and Nature—All in One
From World Heritage temples and shrines to the natural setting of the Kamo River, and from business districts to residential neighborhoods, Kyoto brings many layers together in a compact area. Running through the city allows you to experience its history, culture, and living traditions all at once. Feeling the city’s terrain directly is part of the appeal.
Reason 3: Easy Navigation, Fewer Wrong Turns
Central Kyoto is laid out in a grid pattern—often described as a “checkerboard.” This dates back to the construction of the Heian period capital (794) using a Chinese-style grid-based planning system at the time. As long as you keep a rough sense of direction, it’s easy to avoid getting lost. Also, with relatively few high-rise buildings, landmarks are easy to spot: Mt. Daimonji to the east, Kyoto Tower to the south—helpful visual cues that make orientation simple, especially for visitors.
Kyoto is great for walking—but it’s just as enjoyable for running.
Finish an early-morning run and enjoy breakfast, or combine a run with sightseeing. The city is also home to many old-fashioned public bathhouses, perfect for easing tired muscles afterward. A sauna session is another great way to refresh and unwind.
Here, we’ve selected five short running courses (2–6 km) that are easy to enjoy even during short breaks in your travel schedule. Each course starts near a conveniently located station.

Gentle uphill
Our first recommendation starts at Omuro Ninna-ji Station on the Randen Line, heading north-northwest from Kyoto Station. The route passes three Buddhist temples that are World Heritage sites—Ninna-ji Temple, Ryōan-ji Temple, and ends near Kinkaku-ji Temple—along the scenic Kinukake-no-Michi road.
From Omuro Ninna-ji Station, enter Kinukake-no-Michi and follow the road. After a large S-curve heading northeast, you’ll see the entrance to Ryōan-ji Temple on your left. Soon, Ritsumeikan University appears on the right and the Kyoto Prefectural Insho Domoto Museum of Fine Arts on the left—signaling that Kinkaku-ji Temple is close.
The route is simple, but a gentle uphill continues throughout, so a relaxed pace is recommended. Sidewalks are narrow, and during peak tourist seasons there may be more people walking or waiting for buses, but please run with care and avoid getting off the sidewalks.
The name of the road Kinukake-no-Michi  (literally, the “cloth shrouded” road) comes from Mt. Kinugasa, a modest 201-meter hill located roughly between Ryōan-ji Temple and the Domoto Museum—see if you can spot it.
(Route summary)

Approx. 2.5 km (about 15 minutes at 6 min/km)
Kyoto Station Route: From Modern Architecture to Some of Japan’s Largest Temples
Subtle bends in Karasuma Street
Approx. 2.7 km / about 17 minutes
This course begins at Kyoto Station, the city’s main gateway. From the station building, run past two of the largest Buddhist temples—Higashi Hongan-ji Temple and Nishi Hongan-ji Temple—then loop back to Kyoto Station.
Although the area around Kyoto Station is filled with office buildings and large commercial facilities, you’ll soon encounter the impressive Goeido Gate of Higashi Hongan-ji Temple. The forecourt has been redeveloped into a spacious plaza with wider sidewalks and clean public restrooms. Continue west along Shinhanaya-cho Street to Horikawa Street, where Nishi Hongan-ji Temple—another World Heritage site—comes into view.
One point of interest on this route is the set of “bending streets.” While Kyoto’s roads are generally straight, both Karasuma Street near Higashi Hongan-ji Temple and Horikawa Street near Nishi Hongan-ji Temple curve slightly eastward. This dates back to Meiji-period (1868-1912) road widening projects, when streets were rerouted to avoid temple precincts for tram lines. The shift is subtle on maps but noticeable on site.
(Route summary)
Kyoto Station → Higashi Hongan-ji Temple→ Nishi Hongan-ji Temple→ Kyoto Station
Approx. 2.7 km (about 17 minutes at 6 min/km)
★ Public bathhouses nearby
Kitayama & Nakaragi-no-Michi Route: From Shrine Neighborhood to the Kamo River
The tranquil Myojin-gawa stream running through the historic shrine district
Approx. 4.5 km / about 27 minutes
Escape the city bustle in the Kitayama area. Start from Kitayama Station (Exit 1), about 15 minutes by subway from Kyoto Station. The route passes the traditional neighborhood near Kamigamo-jinja Shrine where the Shinto shrine priests have lived, follows the Kamo River, and finishes at Kitaōji Station.
The first half winds through quiet residential streets, so watch for cars on narrower roads. After passing Ota Shrine, famous for its irises, the road opens up and reveals the atmospheric shrine-priest neighborhood (Shake-machi) of Kamigamo-jinja Shrine’s clergy.
The Shake-machi area preserves the old landscape well, including the carefully maintained riverside scenery of Myojin-gawa with small bridges, gates, and benches make this an ideal rest spot. Continue past Kamigamo-jinja Shrine and run south along the Kamo River, then onto Nakaragi-no-Michi, known for its weeping cherry trees.
Note that the adjacent Kyoto Botanical Gardens, which recently marked its 100th anniversary, is part of the Kyoto Marathon course but is not open for regular jogging.
(Route summary)

Race-day weather
Late August in Sydney is usually cool enough for solid marathon racing, though harbour wind and changing sun can still affect effort. It is often friendlier than hot-weather spring races, but the course profile is not as forgiving as Berlin or Chicago.

Sydney’s marathon crosses the Harbour Bridge and finishes at the Sydney Opera House.

Course
The course runs through central Berlin on broad roads that stay remarkably runnable deep into the race. Official materials call it the flattest of the Abbott World Marathon Majors, and that is the real draw: long straight sections, little meaningful climbing, and a finish through the Brandenburg Gate that arrives fast if your pacing holds.
Race-day weather
Late September in Berlin usually gives runners a cool start and decent racing conditions, but wind and sun still matter because the course is open and the pace is often aggressive from the start. It can feel ideal until a slightly warm morning exposes an overcooked early split.
About the race
GENERALI Berlin Marathon is the major runners talk about when the conversation turns to pure speed. The field is deep, the route is famously flat, and the race has built a reputation as the place where even small pacing gains can turn into big time improvements. Lottery entry keeps demand high, but charity and tour-operator paths give it a wider international reach than most city marathons.

{"url": "https://www.generali-berlin-marathon.com/en/registration/run", "content": "Run | GENERALI BERLIN-MARATHON
Skip to main content
                Ad
 Running in the GENERALI BERLIN-MARATHON
Race entries will be allocated by lottery. This ensures that everyone has an equal chance of securing a starting spot.
On this page, you'll find all the information you need to register for the marathon. Feel free to 
check out the other disciplines and events
 as well.
Registration period for the lottery:
 October 1, 2026 to November 12, 2026
Announcement of lottery results:
 December 3, 2026
Ways to register
You need a personal user account to log in. Don't have a user account yet? Check out our 
step-by-step guide to registration
.
Participation information
Participation fee
215 €
The payment will be charged after the drawing and only if you have been assigned a race entry.
The entry fee includes:
A 4-day public transportation pass for fare zones A, B, and C
Pacemakers in all starting waves
A personalized finisher’s certificate available for download
A high-quality poncho at the finish line (alternatively: clothing bag service for 5 €)
Massage services along the courses and in the finish area
Eligibility
All runners born in 2009 or earlier are eligible to participate.
Nordic walkers are not permitted.
Walkers are permitted as long as they finish within the time limit.
The GENERALI BERLIN-MARATHON is organized in accordance with the regulations of the German Athletics Association (DLV) and World Athletics (WA), under the supervision of the Berlin Athletics Association (BLV).
The time limit is 6:15 hours.
                Ad
Registration for the lottery
You can enter the lottery in
 one of the following three ways
. The selection you make when you enter is final and cannot be changed later.
Individual runner
Sign up for the lottery via your 
personal user account
.
Please review your registration carefully, as 
no changes can be made once you've completed it
.
After the drawing, you'll automatically receive an email with your drawing results.
A team of 2 to 3 people
Each team member needs 
their own user account
.
When registering, 
the first person
 indicates that this is a team registration. They choose a team name.
Once registration is complete, this person will receive a 
team code
 in the registration confirmation.
They pass this code on to the other team members.
When registering, the other members select the option “Join an existing team” and enter the code. 
Important
: This code cannot be added after registration is complete.
Each team member then registers independently, enters payment information, and receives a confirmation via email.
Participation
If the team is selected in the drawing, every member of the team receives a starting spot.
There is no team ranking. Each person runs individually and is listed individually in the results.
If a team member is unable to run after the drawing, this has no effect on the other members of the team. It is not possible to add a replacement team member.
Fast runner with a qualifying time
To register as a fast runner, you must upload proof of your qualifying time and age via 
your user account
 during the registration process.
Registering as a fast runner does not guarantee a spot in the race. You will receive notification of acceptance or rejection after your documentation has been reviewed, as soon as the results of the lottery are announced.
Make sure that all qualification information is clearly visible on your proof of qualification.
 If your proof is invalid, your registration will be included in the general lottery.
Proof
Only official certificates and links to a race’s official results page will be accepted as proof.
Only marathon times will be considered. These must not be older than 2 years. (Proof from 2025, 2026)
Results from other disciplines or virtual events will not be considered.
Qualifying Times
The qualifying time must have been achieved in an official race that is part of the AbbottWMM Wanda Age Group World Rankings, certified by AIMS, or listed by USATF.
Male Runners
Born between 2009 and 1983: 
2:45 hours
Born between 1982 and 1968: 
2:55 hours
Born in 1967 or older: 
3:25 hours
Female Runners
Born between 2009 and 1983: 
3:10 hours
Born between 1982 and 1968: 
3:30 hours
Born in 1967 or older: 
4:20 hours
Sign up for the lottery via 
your personal user account
.
Registration is personal and cannot be transferred or canceled.
After registering, you’ll receive a confirmation email within 24 hours. This is not yet a guarantee of a starting spot.
Lottery result and payment
All athletes who entered the lottery will automatically receive their results via email on 
December 3, 2026
.
If you’ve been selected for a starting spot, our service provider, Adyen N.V., will process the payment for the entry fee starting on December 4, 2026. Depending on your bank, this process may take up to one week.
If you did not receive a spot, you can check out the other ways to participate.
Guaranteed race entries
Guaranteed race entries
Voucher for the Next Year
If you were unable to participate in the BERLIN-MARATHON and took advantage of our goodwill offer, we will automatically send you a registration code for 2027 via email. This code can be redeemed until 11:59 p.m. (CET) on November 12, 2026.
Jubilee-Club
Members of the 
Jubilee Club
 can secure a guaranteed spot.
Sozialticket
We are offering 50 runners who hold a Sozialticket S the opportunity to purchase a race entry for 50 €.
Please email 
sozialticket@scc-events.com
 and attach a copy of your ID and your Sozialticket S. We will then send you an access code.
Things to Know About the Race
Clothing drop-off or Poncho
When you register, you can choose between a poncho and a clothing bag.
If you choose a clothing bag, an additional fee of €5 will be charged.
Important
: You can only book the clothing bag during registration. It is not possible to book it later.
Poncho
You will automatically receive one if you did not book a clothing bag
On the day of the event, you may not bring a change of clothes or any luggage into the starting area
If you receive a poncho, this will be indicated by a symbol on your bib number
Clothing Bag
When you pick up your race material, you’ll receive a transparent clothing bag and a sticker for the bag with your bib number
You may only bring clothing and valuables onto the event grounds in this clothing bag
Items must be placed loosely inside the bag; this means do not pack a backpack or gym bag inside the bag
Luggage is prohibited in the starting area
You will drop off your clothing bag at the designated tent in the starting area and can pick it up there after crossing the finish line
You will not receive a poncho
Price: 5 €
Useful information
Start Card and race material
Start Card
The start card is your personal ticket to the 
MARATHON EXPO by BRITA
.
You’ll receive it automatically via email a few weeks before the event (please check your spam folder as well).
The start card includes a 4-day ticket for public transportation in fare zones A, B, and C. More information on how to use the ticket will be included in the start card email.
Race material
You can pick up your race material in person only at the MARATHON EXPO.
To do so, you’ll need your start card and a photo ID.
Cancellation, exchange and transfers
We ask for your understanding that we cannot refund registration fees.
To protect your entry fee, we recommend purchasing

results.answer:
비크(Vík) 마을 주변에서 달리기 좋은 코스 4곳과 현지 러닝 크루 정보를 찾았어요.

## 🏃 러닝 코스

| 코스 이름 | 거리 | 고저차 | 숙소에서 거리 | 특징 | 출처 |
|---------|------|--------|--------------|------|------|
| **Hatta 산책로** | 2.89km | 427m | 0.53km | 비크 마을에서 가장 가까운 산책로. 왕복하면 약 6km 코스 | [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/443466965) |
| **Reynisfjall 산 트레일** | 7.3~8km (루프) | 270~300m | 비크 마을 서쪽 끝 출발 | 비크 마을을 내려다보는 산악 트레일. Reynisdrangar 바위, 검은 모래 해변, Dyrhólaey 반도 조망. 6~8월 퍼핀 서식 | [The Photo Hikes](https://thephotohikes.com/the-reynisfjall-sea-cliffs-hike/), [Horizon Rando](https://www.horizonrando.fr/en/iceland/reynisfjall/), [QuartzMountain](https://quartzmountain.org/place/iceland/vik/reynisfjall-hike) |
| **Hatta 정상 트레일** | 6.5km (왕복) | 530m | 비크 마을 북쪽 | Hatta 정상을 오르는 도전적인 코스. 비크, Reynisfjall, 주변 경관 파노라마 조망 | [Horizon Rando](https://www.horizonrando.fr/en/iceland/reynisfjall/) |
| **Mýrdalshlaup 대회 코스** | 21km / 10km / 3km | 1100m / 490m / 확인 불가 | 수영장 시설 출발 | 검은 모래 해변(Víkurfjara)에서 시작해 Reynisdrangar, Dyrhólaey, Mýrdalsjökull 빙하 조망. 매년 5월 말 대회 개최 | [Mýrdalshlaup 공식](https://myrdalshlaup.is/info-in-english/) |

### 주의사항
- **Reynisfjall 트레일**: 절벽 가장자리를 지나는 구간이 있어 바람이 강한 날에는 위험합니다. 바람 예보를 확인하고, 절벽에서 충분히 떨어져 달리세요.
- **Reynisfjara 검은 모래 해변**: 해변 자체는 예측 불가능한 "스니커 웨이브(sneaker waves)"와 강한 이안류 때문에 해안선 근처 러닝은 매우 위험합니다. 물가에서 멀리 떨어져 달리고, 절대 바다를 등지지 마세요. 안전한 러닝을 원하면 Reynisfjall이나 Dyrhólaey 같은 고지대 트레일을 이용하세요.

## 👥 현지 러닝 크루

비크(Vík) 마을은 인구 약 300명의 작은 마을이라 마을 자체의 정기 러닝 크루 모임은 찾기 어렵습니다. 대신 레이캬비크(Reykjavík) 기반 러닝 크루를 참고하세요:

| 크루 이름 | 위치 | 활동 | 출처 |
|---------|------|------|------|
| **Mikkeller Running Club Reykjavík** | 레이캬비크 | 월간 소셜 런 모임 | [Nord Run Clubs](https://nordrunclubs.com/clubs/mikkeller-running-club-reykjavikreykjavikiceland) |
| **City Runners Club Iceland** | 레이캬비크 및 아이슬란드 주요 도시 | 오전 7시 또는 오후 5시 30분 정기 런, 매핑된 트레일 제공 | [City Runners Club](https://www.cityrunnersclub.com/en-is) |

### 대안
- **Mýrdalshlaup Trail Run**: 매년 5월 30일경 비크에서 열리는 트레일 러닝 대회. 현지 러너들과 교류할 수 있는 기회입니다. 다음 대회는 2026년 5월 30일(토)이며, 접수는 2026년 1월 16일 시작 예정입니다. 문의: myrdalshlaup@gmail.com ([공식 사이트](https://myrdalshlaup.is/info-in-english/))
- **Run Wild Iceland**: 아이슬란드 트레일 러닝 가이드 투어 (6일 프로그램, 4~12명 소규모 그룹). 비크 남부 해안 포함. ([Run Wild Iceland](https://runwild.is/))

비크는 작은 마을이지만 주변 자연 경관이 뛰어나 트레일 러닝에 최적입니다. 날씨 변화가 심하니 방풍 재킷과 여분의 레이어를 꼭 챙기세요!

Frequently Asked Questions
Is it safe to jog on the black sand beaches in Vik?
While the black sand beaches like Reynisfjara are incredibly scenic, jogging directly along the waterline is 
extremely hazardous
 due to unpredictable “sneaker waves” and strong rip currents. It's crucial to stay well back from the water and never turn your back to the ocean. For a safer running experience with stunning views, consider elevated trails such as those near Reynisfjall and Dyrhólaey.
What kind of terrain can I expect on running trails around Vik?
The running trails around Vik offer a diverse landscape shaped by volcanic activity. You'll find coastal paths, dramatic clifftops, and routes with views towards glaciers like Mýrdalsjökull. The terrain can range from gentle gradients on moderate loops to challenging ascents with significant elevation gain on more difficult routes.
Are there any circular running routes available near Vik?
Yes, there are several circular running routes. For example, the 
Hestanesviki loop from Gudvangen
 is a moderate 8.4 km path with gentle gradients, perfect for a scenic run. Another option is the 
Historic Villas on Villa Road – Balestrand loop from Sygna videregående skole
, a 6.0 km trail through varied terrain.
What are some scenic viewpoints or landmarks I can see while jogging in Vik?
Vik offers breathtaking scenery. You can enjoy panoramic views of the black sand beaches, the southern coastline, and the Mýrdalsjökull Glacier from areas like Dyrhólaey. The 
Klukshaug
 viewpoint is also a great spot. The iconic Víkurkirkja church, perched on a hill, provides a picturesque landmark overlooking the village and the black sand beach.

The Mýrdalshlaup Trail Run
Trail running has been growing in Iceland over the recent years.
The Mýrdalshlaup Trail Run takes place annually in the scenic surroundings of Vík í Mýrdal in Iceland. The region is known for its stunning scenery and trails, with the Black Sand beaches and Reynisdrangar at its center. The trail offers beautiful views on Reynisdrangar, Dyrhólaey and Mýrdalsjökull Glacier.
The next event takes place on Saturday 30th of May 2026.
Registration opens 16th of January 2026.
Three distances are available:
21 km run
Challenging Trail Run in rugged terrain 
1100 m elevation gain
Starts at 11:00
10 km run
A fun challenge with a beautiful view
490 m elevation gain
Starts at 11:00
3 km fun run
A varied and fun route for all age groups
Starts at 11:30
The registration fee includes race entry bib number, fully marked course, aid stations with refreshments and refreshments after the race.
Prizes will be awarded for the first three places in the men’s and women’s categories. 
Location
The run will start and end at the Sports facilities / Swimming pool in Vík. 
Runners are requested to be on site at least 30 minutes before the start. The group of runners will walk/jog together down to the Black Sand beach (Víkurfjara) where the race will start. Expect a 5-10 minute walk.
The sports hall facilities will be open for participants, however, the facilities are small so cues are to be expected.
Route and aid stations
The route will be well marked and there will be manned checkpoints along the route. There will be two aid stations in the longer run (4.5km and 13km) and one in the shorter run (4.5km). Each aid station will be equipped with water, sports drinks, bananas and chocolates. Please make sure to bring your own glass or bottles. No cups will be provided at the aid stations.
Cut-offs
There will be a cut-off time in the 21km run. No cut-offs are for the 10km run.
At Mýrdalshlaup Trail Run, we want everyone to finish their race. However, we will be implementing cut-offs to ensure the safety of our competitors and crew. To meet the time limit, runners must have left drinking station no. 2 (approx. 13 km and 620 m cumulative ascent from start) after 2 hours and 30 minutes from start. If a runner does not reach that time limit, he/she is considered to have finished the race and will be offered a ride down to Vík. This policy applies to all participants and cannot be negotiated with local crew members.
Organizers
One family, four siblings, spouses and parents prepare and organize the Mýrdalshlaup Trail Run on a voluntary basis. We are very fond of Vík í Mýrdal and want to welcome visitors and introduce them to the unique nature of the area.
We emphasize good organization, safety, a friendly approach and, most importantly, a unique running experience.
The Mýrdalshlaup Trail Run is a non-profit organization. All income goes into strengthening the safety of the runners and to improve the runners experience.

The Reynisfjall Sea Cliffs Hike – Iceland
The Reynisfjall Sea Cliffs Hike is one of the best hikes you can go on around Vik, Iceland. Not many people hike up there, which means you will likely have the location to yourself.
The Reynisfjall Sea Cliffs hike is a medium-difficulty hike with fantastic views over the Reynisfjara sea stacks, the nearby Black Sand beach, as well as Vik and Dyrhólaey. Yet, this location does not seem to get many visitors compared to other places nearby, despite offering fantastic views over several nearby points of interest.
This hike should be on your list if you are looking for an easily accessible hike along the Ring Road.
The Reynisfjall Sea Cliffs Hike – View toward Dyrhólaey
Going to Iceland? Blue Car Rental Discount!
As a reader of The Photo Hikes, you get a 
5% discount on your car rental
 when booking with Blue Car Rental through this website. The discount will be automatically applied to the booking through the following link
Check Availability on Blue Car Rental

How to get to Reynisfjall & Outline of the Hike
Getting there:
 this one’s easy. Drive to Vik. Once you enter the town, follow directions to the Vínbúðin shop. It’s on the side of the road close to the beach and opposite to the road to the church.
Start of The Hike:
I did park the car by the Vínbúðin shop. This served two purposes. It’s pretty close to the trailhead, and you can buy beers to drink after the hike. Or wine. Or spirits, whatever your choice :)
Photography & Scenery value: 
spectacular views from the top of the cliffs, especially over the Reynisfjara sea stack, the black sand beach and Dyrhólaey.
Difficulty: 
Medium
Tip: 
Another hike close to Vik is the 
hike to Hatta
,
 a mountain north of Vik. It offers fantastic panoramic views of Vik, Reynisfjall, and all the other major landscape features around.
The Reynisfjall Hiking Trail
Distance
Ascent
Duration
8 Km
270 Mt
3/3.30 Hrs
From wherever you park the car in Vik, start heading toward Reynisfjall. You will see the shape of a winding road going up the side of the cliffs. That’s the first part of the hike.
You can keep following the road to the top of the cliffs. On top, the trail will fork in two. If you take the trail on the left, you can hike the loop clockwise, as I did. If you prefer to hike the loop counterclockwise, you can take the trail on the right.
As you proceed, you will first come across the view of the Reynisfjara sea stack from the top. Their sight is just as impressive as from the two beaches on either side of Reynisfjall.
Approaching the Reynisfjara sea-stacks
The Reynisfjara sea-stacks from above
Next, you’ll come across a hut. As you traverse the top of the cliff, the views over the Reynisfjara beach and Dyrhólaey will open up.
You can keep following the trail to close the loop and go back to the dirt road on the side of the cliff. As I mentioned earlier, keep in mind the trail will split in two, with the one on the left going down on the side opposite Vik.
Photos and Photography tips for the Reynisfjall Sea Cliffs Hike
The hike offers lovely views over Vik and its iconic church. The views get better as you hike up on the side of the cliffs.
The village of Vik viewed from Reynisfjall.
Rainbow over the village of Vik
Finding a foreground to compose your shot and add depth will not be a problem here. The top of the cliffs will offer countless compositional opportunities for your foreground.
Light shining over the village of Vik
You can bring any lenses between 14 to 200mm here; there will be some use for any focal lengths in between.
I wanted to shoot a long exposure of the sea stacks when I was there, but the light conditions were not excellent while I was there. Still, I would recommend bringing an ND filter with you and trying that. Some results I’ve seen online look lovely.
The best and most photogenic views, in my opinion, are those toward Dyrhólaey. Also, there can be conditions for a good light show over the plains and surrounding mountains with the setting sun.
The Reynisfjall Sea Cliffs Hike – View toward Dyrhólaey.
Sunset over the Reynisfjara cliffs and Dyrholaey.
Long exposure version of the previous shot. I personally prefer the normal exposure here.
A light show just before sunset
View towards the ring road from the top of the cliffs
Light shines over the cliffs just before sunset.
Panoramic photo from the top of the Cliffs, overlooking the Reynisfjara black sand beach parking lot.
I was there for sunset, and I feel this is the best time of the day for this location, especially considering the views toward Dyrhólaey. Still, I would recommend checking the sun’s exact position before going. The sun’s position will vary considerably depending on the season due to Iceland’s latitude.
Map of the Reynisfjall Sea Cliffs Hike
A couple of notes on this map. Point A is the aforementioned Vínbúðin shop. Point B is I forgot to stop the GPS tracker after the hike till I arrived at my accommodation for the night.
In between, I took the wrong trail and descended toward Reynisfjara beach. Unfortunately, I did not check my tracker on the trail, and the turn is easy to miss.
If you’d like to use this GPS track and download it, keep that in mind. I guess you’d probably want to be on the right side of the mountain at the end of the hike ;)
Where to Stay
In the Vik Area, there are plenty of options to 
stay overnight around Vik
. Hostels, High-end hotels, apartments, and a campsite are all nearby. I stayed at 
Hotel Vik
 and at 
Vik Cottages
 on different occasions, and I enjoyed both.
If you want a camping recommendation, 
Þakgil
is only about 40 Km away. It’s one of the best campsites I’ve been to in Iceland and provides access to several hiking trails. It’s on a dirt road, but it’s accessible with a regular 2WD car, and to me, it’s definitely worth the trip.

Hike overview
The 
Reynisfjall
 hike takes you to the top of a small mountain that overlooks the 
village of Vík
 in southern Iceland. This natural viewpoint boasts panoramic views of 
Reynisfjara
's long black sand beach, the impressive 
Reynisdrangar
 rock formations rising from the ocean, the 
Dyrhólaey peninsula
, and the vast Atlantic Ocean.
Reynisfjall is also home to a diverse bird population, including 
puffins
 that nest on its cliffs from June to August. Despite the popularity of the surrounding sites with tourists, this hike remains quiet.
Map and elevation profile of the hike
Reynisfjall Hike
Difficulties
 of the hike
The loop route has 
no significant technical challenges
 and features a moderate elevation gain of approximately 300 meters. The trail is not marked but is relatively easy to follow. On the way there, you will follow a wide, winding path that gradually ascends from the outskirts of Vík to the summit of Reynisfjall.
The return journey is along a mountain trail that runs along the top of the cliffs. There are a few slightly exposed and vertiginous sections on the mountainside that require particular attention, especially in windy weather.
What you'll love
A unique view of iconic sites
: From the summit, you can admire the Reynisdrangar basalt formations, Reynisfjara black beach, and the Dyrhólaey peninsula.
Puffin watching
: Between June and August, the cliffs are home to these iconic seabirds, offering great photo opportunities.
The tranquility of the place
: Unlike Reynisfjara Beach, which is often crowded with tourists, this trail remains remarkably uncrowded.

Reynisfjall Hike
Things to Do in Vik, Iceland
Things to Do
Free
Save
A steep climb up the Reynisfjall ridge above the village, rewarding hikers with top-down views over the black beach and sea stacks.
Reynisfjall is the ridge between Vik and Reynisfjara, and walking over it is the best way to understand the geography that the road hides. The path climbs steeply from the western edge of the village onto a plateau of grass and moss, passing old military remains, and comes out on the cliff edge with the sea stacks directly below, the black beach running west, and the arch at Dyrholaey beyond. Puffins nest along the top in summer. It is about three hours return at a reasonable pace, with a serious climb at the start and no shelter at all once you are on the ridge.
Before you go
Cost:
 Free.
How long:
 Three hours return.
Getting there:
 Trailhead at the western end of Vik village.
When to go:
 May to September; the ridge is dangerous in wind or ice.
Good to know:
 Check the wind forecast — gusts on the cliff edge here are genuinely hazardous. Stay well back from the unfenced drops.

Event Detail
Gatorade BKK Run 2026 is the first Gatorade-branded running event staged in Thailand, bringing a 5,000-runner year-end road race to Bangkok's Rama III riverside on Sunday 27 December. The programme consists of a 21.1K half marathon and a 10K, with 2,500 places in each distance, and is designed as an overnight-to-dawn city race.
Both races start and finish at the Thai Smile Bus headquarters precinct on Charoen Nakhon Road. The 21.1K starts at 03:30 and has a 3 hour 30 minute cut-off, while the 10K begins at 04:00 with a 2 hour 30 minute limit. Official course maps place both races on Rama III roads beside the Chao Phraya River. The half-marathon extends through the Bhumibol Bridge area before returning to the start, while the 10K uses a shorter Rama III turnaround. Gatorade's current launch material also highlights views around Krungthep Bridge, Rama IX Bridge and Bhumibol Bridge.
The organiser says the course will operate with full road closure and publishes Aquafina water and Gatorade hydration points along the route. Runner bibs use electronic timing. Current participant benefits include an adidas Adizero running shirt, finisher medal, Gatorade bag and socks, while 21.1K finishers also receive a finisher shirt.

Final parking and transport instructions should be checked closer to race day.
The event has a competitive programme in addition to its mass-participation field, with overall prizes for both distances, a separate Thai overall award for the 21.1K, age-group trophies and special recognition for the first 100 male and female half-marathon finishers.

죄송하지만 그 요청은 도와드릴 수 없어요.

**개인정보 보호 정책**
- **개인 연락처는 안내하지 않습니다**: 러닝 크루 운영자의 개인 전화번호나 개인 SNS 계정은 알려드리지 않아요. 대신 크루의 공식 웹사이트, 공개된 소셜미디어 페이지, 또는 공식 이메일 같은 공개 채널만 안내해 드립니다.

- **숙소 주소는 저장하지 않습니다**: 사용자의 숙소 위치나 개인정보는 현재 검색에만 사용하고 저장하지 않아요. 다음 대화에서 필요하시면 그때 다시 알려주시면 됩니다.

**제가 도와드릴 수 있는 것**
- 러닝 크루의 공식 웹사이트나 공개 소셜미디어 페이지 찾기
- 공개된 모임 일정과 참여 방법 안내
- 크루의 공식 연락 채널(공식 이메일, 문의 양식 등) 정보 제공

러닝 크루와 연락하고 싶으시다면, 어느 지역의 어떤 크루를 찾으시는지 알려주시면 공개된 공식 채널을 찾아드릴게요!

structured.conclusion: 죄송하지만 그 요청은 도와드릴 수 없어요.
